problem_markdown: In regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, points $M\in AC$ and $N\in CE$ satisfy $AM/AC=CN/CE=r$, with $0<r<1$. Determine $r$ when $B,M,N$ are collinear.
solutions_markdown:
Use coordinates $A=(1,0)$, $B=(1/2,\sqrt3/2)$, $C=(-1/2,\sqrt3/2)$ and $E=(-1/2,-\sqrt3/2)$. Then
$$M=(1-3r/2,\sqrt3r/2),\qquad N=(-1/2,\sqrt3(1-2r)/2).$$
The determinant of $M-B$ and $N-B$ equals
$$(1/2-3r/2)(-\sqrt3r)-(\sqrt3(r-1)/2)(-1)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(3r^2-1).$$
It vanishes exactly when $r=\pm1/\sqrt3$. The required interior value is $r=1/\sqrt3$, and substituting it verifies collinearity.
